Synopsis:
Voicebark dialog after robbing the amulet from Jergal chapel, about whether it was right to loot the place. Its guardians might have been killed by the player. Or the guardians might have engaged the player, but they found a way to get out without killing them all, by fleeing or distracting them. Or the player might have sneakily escape the guardians.This is played on the party after they leave an area, so Speakers are roughly interchangeable here, the undertaking is assumed to be a party effort.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_Crypt_PAD_SuccessfulGraverobbing.json: The party has just left a neglected Jergal chapel/tomb after taking an amulet from a statue or altar; a worn bronze plaque at the site is illegible to them (no clear translation or lore has been revealed), so the cult or patron is obscure. Off‑screen the group encountered the chapel’s guardians — they may have killed them, frightened or distracted them, or slipped past without slaying everyone — so who lived or died and exactly how the escape went is left ambiguous. The lines are a post‑raid debate over whether looting the dead was justified and what to do with the relics, not a detailed replay of the fight. Because this is a party voicebark, any companion might speak the lines and they reflect the party’s collective action and attitude rather than a named NPC’s fixed stance.
- LOW_HouseOfHope_TreasureBlocker.json: The dialogue for when players try to pick up the treasure while it's still locked.Through this dialogue players can also remove the defense.Node about the Orphic Hammer should be in sync with LOW_HouseOfHope_AD_Treasure02Plaque dialogue
- CHA_Outside_Bandit_Melee_01_Dead.json: Speak with Dead dialogue with Gimblebock - the leader of the bandits who're looting the ruined chapel near where the player first wakes up. Gimblebock's answers are fragmented, cryptic. He can only draw on info that he knew when he was alive, and will refuse to speak to his killer if he recognises them. After a maximum of five questions, he'll fall silent for good.
- CHA_Outside_BanditBackInteraction_Spotted.json: Right outside of the abandonned chapel of Selune you encounter a few bandits arguing among themselves. They are rightfully surprise to see you get out of the ruins and worried about the fate of their friend inside.
- UND_DuergarCamp_RebelsExtort.json: In this dialogue, you have killed Nere without doing the duergar mutineers quest. As a result, they want you to pay for the trouble you've caused. You can give them money, persuade them to let you live, or attack.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Player: They didn't want to surrender their valuables, even after death. (node 0)

Sample 2:
- Player: I pity anyone caught by those things. We were lucky to get out with the loot. (node 2)

Sample 3:
- Player: A lucky escape. Judging by how they fought, those things weren't happy with our looting. (node 4)
- Player: Relics are wasted on bones. We can make much better use of them. (node 5)

context: The party has just left a neglected Jergal chapel/tomb after taking an amulet from a statue or altar; a worn bronze plaque there is illegible, so the cult or patron remains obscure. Off‑screen the group ran into the chapel’s guardians — it’s left ambiguous whether the party slew them, scared or distracted them, or slipped past without killing everyone. These lines are a post‑raid, party‑wide voicebark debating whether looting the dead was right and what to do with the relics. Any companion might speak them; they reflect the party’s collective action and attitude rather than a single NPC’s fixed stance.
